_comment: Human-maintained fundamentals facts for the article's Q3 (why the Gold Coast is holding up). Migration + affordability are hand-curated from primary sources (each carries its own source + period); jobs come from labour_context.json (ABS API) and the arbitrage from arbitrage_context.json (onthehouse + our data). Refresh migration after each ABS/QGSO release. Every figure below was read from the cited source; do not add a figure without one.

migration.text: Queensland recorded a net interstate migration gain of 21,595 people in 2024–25 — the largest of any state — with the biggest inflows from New South Wales (+13,020) and Victoria (+6,920); New South Wales alone accounted for 60.3% of that net gain
migration.source: Queensland Government Statistician's Office, from ABS

migration.text: Queensland has recorded a net interstate migration gain in every quarter since June 1981 — the only state to do so
migration.source: Queensland Government Statistician's Office, from ABS

migration.text: the Gold Coast was among Australia's fastest-growing regions, expanding 2.3% in 2023–24

affordability.text: a median-income Sydney household needs about 16.7 years to save a 20% deposit, against 12.9 years in Brisbane

drivers_research._comment: Fields' own published lead/lag analysis (articles what-drives-gold-coast-house-prices and leading-vs-lagging-indicators). Figures verified from those articles 2026-08-24. Used in Section 4 to show which indicators lead vs lag GC prices, so current readings can be interpreted.
drivers_research.scope: our analysis of 27 economic series across eight Gold Coast suburbs, 2015–2025
lagging: interest rates follow Gold Coast prices by about a year (they lag, at r = 0.79) — the Reserve Bank moves in response to the economy, not ahead of any one suburb
bank lending lags prices too, by around three to four months
leading: household spending is the single strongest gauge of market strength here (r = 0.91)
Queensland wage growth has run about three to four months ahead of house prices
retail spending, a proxy for confidence, has led by four to five months
drivers_research.income: a 1% rise in real household income has, over the period, moved Gold Coast prices about 1.7%
drivers_research.caveat: these are relationships measured in past data, not forecasts — a lead observed before may not hold again

caveats.gc_overseas_led: In 2023–24 the Gold Coast's own growth leaned more on overseas than interstate migration; the interstate flow is unambiguous at the Queensland level.
caveats.moderating: The interstate inflow is strongly positive but has moderated from its 2020–21 pandemic peak.
